messages.content: How much gas is generated from heating a 2 m³ closed chamber with air at a temperature of 25°C to 100°C?

function.name: thermodynamics_calc_gas_pressure
function.description: Calculate gas pressure in a closed chamber due to heating Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

volume.description: The volume of the chamber in cubic meters. This is a float type value.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the gas in degree Celsius. This is a float type value.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the gas in degree Celsius. This is a float type value.

initial_pressure.description: The initial pressure of the gas in Pascal. Default is standard atmospheric pressure. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "How much gas is generated from heating a 2 m³ closed chamber with air at a temperature of 25°C to 100°C?" They want to know how much gas is generated? But it's a closed chamber; heating will increase pressure but not generate more gas. Maybe they mean how much pressure increases? Or maybe they think heating causes expansion and thus generates more gas? Actually, if it's sealed, no gas generation. So answer: No additional gas is generated; only pressure changes. We can calculate new pressure using ideal gas law: P1V/T1 = P2V/T2 => P2 = P1 * T2/T1. Use absolute temperatures: T1=298K, T2=373K. If initial pressure is standard atmospheric (101325 Pa). Then P2 = 101325*(373/298) ≈ 126,800 Pa. So pressure rises ~25% to about 127 kPa. Volume remains constant. So amount of gas stays same. So answer accordingly.
